solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Steal ID and go by furtively — he always gets the blame

parts.note: to whip is slang for to steal or pinch
a PIN is the personal identification number used with a bank card

indicators.note: moving furtively means shifting about sneakily, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief lifts someone's identity card and slinks off, leaving someone else to take the rap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furtively' makes GBOY from GO BY.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat punished for others' faults: historically a boy beaten in place of a young prince.

clue.text: He quibbles over cost statement of child's horse stabled in more healthy environment

indicators.note: a horse is stabled inside a building, so the horse letters are placed within the other word

parts.note: hale means healthy, so haler is more healthy
gee-gee is nursery talk for a horse, written GG

explanation.surface: A parent argues about the price of a child's pony kept in a healthier spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statement of' tells you GG is how the child says the word for horse; 'environment' just adds to the stabling picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggler is someone who bargains or argues over the price of something.

clue.text: Air rising is observed after expert forecast

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the expert

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A meteorologist notes the air is rising and makes a forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the tune upwards; 'observed' is only a link, and 'after' places that reversed air with 'is' below the expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A prognosis is a prediction of how something, especially an illness, will develop.

clue.text: Wally wastes time on masculine mode of expression

indicators.note: wastes suggests something is used up and lost, so a letter disappears from the word

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool or idiot
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A fool wastes time on some masculine way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wastes' removes T from IDIOT to leave IDIO. In a down clue 'on' puts IDIO above M.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a characteristic turn of phrase, a particular way of expressing things.

clue.text: Perhaps greet us with a wave

definitions.note: a wave of the hand is one movement of that kind, a noun like the answer

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone suggests we might be greeted by a wave of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' makes GESTURE from GREET US.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving the hand is a classic example of a bodily signal made to communicate.

clue.text: In public, athletic club give extravagant display

indicators.note: in places the club letters inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open or public

explanation.surface: An athletic club shows off extravagantly in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to perform with exaggerated, theatrical showiness, overdoing a part.

clue.text: Sailor heard small whispering noise. It's just a dog

parts.note: jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

indicators.note: heard tells us to go by the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a rustle is a soft whispering sound, as of leaves

explanation.surface: A sailor hears a faint rustle and realises it is only a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives RUSSELL, which sounds like RUSTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of small terrier named after the Reverend John Russell, a hunting parson.

clue.text: Maybe one employing lawyer's right to be in court

indicators.note: to be in places the right inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A lawyer's right to appear in court is in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who engages a solicitor or barrister is their customer; 'Maybe' marks one example of such a customer.

clue.text: Briskly declare, one short, then get run out

indicators.note: one short means the word is missing one letter, here its last

parts.note: to allege is to declare or assert
RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricketer speaks briskly when a man short and then gets run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one short' cuts the last E from ALLEGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo.

clue.text: Together with Epstein, resolved to drop one Ecstasy pill

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reconstituted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to drop tells us to remove a letter from the name

parts.note: E is slang for an Ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone goes along with Epstein and decides to give up an Ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drop' removes one of the two Es from EPSTEIN; 'resolved' makes INSTEP from what is left. Epstein might be the Beatles' manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in step with someone means moving in harmony, matching them closely.

clue.text: Framework shaped into a story

parts.note: the fabric of a building is its basic structure or framework

indicators.note: shaped means formed into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frame is worked into the shape of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaped' makes ATION from INTO A.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabrication is a made-up account, an invented tale or lie.

clue.text: Troubled Merlin follows king into citadel

indicators.note: follows puts the jumbled name after the letter for king

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the wizard's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A distressed Merlin trails King Arthur into a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' makes REMLIN from MERLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the fortified complex in central Moscow; the word means fortress or citadel in Russian.

clue.text: Flash: African capital parks opening course for connoisseurs of Marathon?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash

indicators.note: parks means sets aside, so the opening letter of the capital is put out of the way

parts.note: Lusaka is the capital of Zambia

explanation.surface: In a flash an African capital opens its parks to marathon fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Marathon is not the race but the town in Greece, whose people know their national dishes; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a baked Greek dish of aubergine and minced meat, a main course in Greece.

clue.text: Absolute fruitcake! He's lost his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: fruitcake and nutter are both slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a man who has lost his temper is a total nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's lost his head' cuts the first letter from NUTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means complete or total, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Gale starts to sweep over US wilderness destroying trees

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next four words
destroying means wrecking, so the letters of the word trees are scrambled

explanation.surface: A storm sweeps across American wilderness, flattening trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' makes ESTER from TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A southwesterly wind, especially a strong one, is a gale blowing from that quarter.

clue.text: Removed fastenings around instrument with full concentration

indicators.note: around puts the first word round the second

parts.note: to undo buttons or ties is to remove fastenings; undid is the past tense
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician unbuttons around the instrument to play with full concentration.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid not watered down keeps full strength; concentration here means chemical strength.

clue.text: Caught unawares retiring gent is surrounded by posturing prudes

indicators.note: is surrounded by puts the gentleman's title inside the jumbled letters
posturing means striking poses, so the letters of the word take a new arrangement
retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is a polite form of address to a gentleman

explanation.surface: A shy gentleman is caught off guard, surrounded by affected prudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posturing' makes SURPED from PRUDES; 'retiring' turns SIR into RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astonished or taken by surprise is to be caught off guard.

clue.text: About time to take pride, say, over Australian wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier part above the next

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pride is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of a sin

explanation.surface: It takes time to swallow pride over a bottle of Australian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Circle Line goes under rough earth

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes under puts the letter below the rest

parts.note: a round figure is a rough or approximate one

explanation.surface: The London Underground's Circle Line runs beneath rough ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, so the opening two words look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a disc or circular emblem, such as the RAF's target-shaped marking.

clue.text: Flowering tree. In Dordogne it's found in lake

indicators.note: found in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: lac is French for lake
Dordogne is in France, where the word for it is il

explanation.surface: A flowering tree grows at a lake in the Dordogne region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are French: IL is 'it' and LAC is 'lake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub or small tree with fragrant purple or white blossoms.

clue.text: Without acting once, contrive above all to be endearing

indicators.note: contrive means devise or arrange, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without tells us to leave one letter out of the phrase

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for acting; once says only one of the two As goes

explanation.surface: An actor who never performs tries above all to be charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes one A from ABOVE ALL; 'contrive' makes LOVABLE from what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing inspires affection, which is the same as being easy to like.

clue.text: Words of Saint Cyril in translation

indicators.note: in translation means put into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The writings of Saint Cyril are rendered in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in translation' makes LYRICS from S and CYRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrics are the words of a song, as distinct from its music.

clue.text: Leaves service with rake-off to return east

parts.note: a let is a tennis serve that clips the net and is replayed

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings, a rake-off

explanation.surface: A servant leaves, taking a cut of the money and heading back east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns CUT into TUC. 'Leaves' looks like a verb but means foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a salad plant eaten for its leaves.

clue.text: In disgrace, discharge former priest by letter

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-husband
el is the spelled-out name of the letter L

explanation.surface: A former priest is dismissed in disgrace by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is the spelled-out name of the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone out, especially from a school or society, is a dismissal in disgrace.

clue.text: Young creature's always dipping into grant

indicators.note: dipping into puts one word inside the other

parts.note: to let is to grant or allow
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A young animal is always dipping into its allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year.

clue.text: Empty words in court irritate

parts.note: wind is empty talk, hot air
up can mean before a court, as in up before the magistrate

explanation.surface: Pointless talk in a courtroom gets on people's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' means appearing before a court, as in being up before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is British slang for annoying or teasing them.

clue.text: Smoke ruined boat caught in banks of Congo

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its edges, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A wrecked boat is stuck between the banks of the Congo, with smoke rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' makes TOBA from BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke is informal for something to smoke, especially tobacco.

clue.text: Organ's grand rendition of Latin ballad before Duke and Queen

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: a rendition is a version or interpretation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A grand performance of a Latin ballad is played for a duke and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendition of' makes ALLBLAD from L and BALLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The gall bladder is an internal body part storing bile beside the liver.
